plain: A person who disagrees with the official or majority view, often in religion.

webster.text: One who dissents; one who differs in opinion, or one who declares his disagreement.

example.quote: Other opinions began then to creep in, and the great care of the government to support their own church, having begotten an equal degree of indolence in its clergy, two-thirds of the people had become dissenters at the commencement of the present revolution.
example.cite: Thomas Jefferson, Notes on the State of Virginia, Query XVII (Religion) (1802 ed.)
